findings.title: Unbounded per-tick stat-walk of archive_status, now on the always-on verbose panel, with no hard bound and an incomplete measurement plan
findings.description:
Decision 8 + Decision 9 put an unthrottled privileged directory walk on the always-on path. Evidence for the cost: pg_ls_archive_statusdir() is pg_ls_dir_files(fcinfo, XLOGDIR "/archive_status", true), which performs a stat() per directory entry (values[1] = st_size, values[2] = st_mtime); pg_ls_dir(), the function being replaced, is readdir-only. collectOverviewStat runs it as its own QueryRow every verbose tick, sequentially with the other aggregates on a single connection, so its latency adds directly to tick latency and (via the unbuffered viewCh) to view-switch latency. The existing latency-guard machinery (latencyGuardThreshold, internal/stat/stat.go:65-76; dbSizeThrottled at stat.go:410, with a proven stale-value degradation path) covers only the db-size aggregate and is not extended here.

Calibration, in the spec's favour: OverviewWalSize (internal/query/overview.go:67) already runs pg_ls_waldir() -- an identical stat-walk over a directory of the same cardinality -- on every verbose tick, unguarded. So this is roughly a 2x increase of an already-unbounded cost, not a new class, which supports the decision to measure before bounding.

What is not covered by that argument, and is the actual gap: for a role holding pg_monitor but not superuser -- the intended monitoring role, and precisely the role Decision 8 exists to serve -- the backlog query today fails instantly with 42501, costing nothing. After the change it succeeds and pays the full walk. The verbose panel's filesystem cost for that role therefore goes from one walk to two, from a baseline of zero for this aggregate. A stand run performed as superuser measures the wrong baseline and will understate the change for the majority deployment. The same walk also runs in pgcenter record independently of which screen is open, because the recorder executes every registered view's query each tick (record/recorder.go:134-142 iterates over all views), so the archiver query's walk is unconditional there.
findings.location: Section: Decision 8, Decision 9, Risks table; internal/stat/postgres.go:292; internal/query/overview.go:100-102
findings.impact: During the exact incident the feature is built for (archiving stalled, archive_status growing without bound, disk likely under pressure), every pgcenter TUI instance with verbose on and every pgcenter record instance pays two full stat-walks of directories that grow with the incident, once per tick per instance, with no upper bound and no timeout. The monitoring tool amplifies load on a cluster already in trouble and can stall its own refresh and view switching, i.e. it degrades exactly when it is most needed. Not remotely exploitable -- it requires an existing connection with pg_monitor -- so this is an availability property, not an attack surface.
findings.recommendation:
Keep the measure-first decision, but close two gaps rather than leaving the outcome to an unspecified measurement:
1. Pin the measurement conditions in Task 10 so the number is meaningful: run as a role with pg_monitor and WITHOUT superuser, with the verbose panel enabled, and with a concurrent pgcenter record. Record the per-query latency of both the backlog aggregate and OverviewWalSize on the ~200 000 .ready directory, plus total tick latency and view-switch latency.
2. Pre-commit to an outcome instead of to a re-opened debate. The bound already exists and is cheap to apply: extend verboseCollectState / latencyGuardThreshold to the backlog source exactly as it is applied to the db-size aggregate (skip next tick when the last run exceeded max(25% of refresh, 500ms), reuse the cached value, force-collect after one refresh interval to re-probe). If the numbers come back acceptable and no guard is added, record the unbounded per-tick walk as a tech-debt entry so it stays a tracked decision rather than an artifact of a measurement that was never run against the right role.

findings.title: Privilege-failure error text is safe as designed, but formatError is a second unsanitised terminal sink not covered by debt [029]
findings.description:
Decision 4 lets the privilege failure take down the whole screen. Assessing what that puts on screen: top/stat.go:859-870 (formatError) prints pgErr.Severity, pgErr.Message, pgErr.Detail and pgErr.Hint verbatim into the gocui view with no SGR wrapper and no escaping. For the failure mode Decision 4 actually produces, the content is 'permission denied for function pg_ls_archive_statusdir' -- it discloses the name of a function the operator just invoked, and nothing else: no filesystem path, no connection string, no query text, no credentials. Decision 4's error exposure is therefore acceptable as designed and needs no change.

Two residuals worth recording. First, pg_ls_dir_files errors with errmsg("could not stat file \"%s\": %m", path) and only skips ENOENT, so a non-ENOENT stat failure inside archive_status is a route by which a filesystem-supplied file name reaches formatError unsanitised. That requires write access to $PGDATA as the postgres user, at which point the operator has larger problems -- it is the same 'needs a hostile name to matter' class as debt [029], on a different sink. Second, debt [029] is scoped to top/stat.go printDataCell only; formatError is a distinct unsanitised sink on the same terminal and is currently recorded nowhere.

Separately, the doc comment being carried forward is now stale: internal/query/overview.go:97-99 and internal/stat/postgres.go:288-290 both justify swallowing the error with 'the raw error (which contains a filesystem path)'. After Decision 8 the query passes no path argument, so that rationale no longer describes the code.
findings.impact: No exposure from the designed failure path. The residual is that the project's record of unsanitised terminal sinks is incomplete, so a future change that routes richer server text through formatError would not be recognised as touching a known-unsanitised surface.
findings.recommendation: No code change in this feature. Extend debt item [029] with a sentence naming top/stat.go formatError as the second unsanitised sink (PgError Severity/Message/Detail/Hint written raw), so both sinks live in one entry. In Task 3, update the swallow-the-error comments at internal/query/overview.go:97-99 and internal/stat/postgres.go:288-290 to state the new reason the error is discarded (it no longer carries a path; the field degrades to n/a on 42501 or a missing function) instead of copying the path-based rationale forward.

findings.title: New server-text columns (last_archived, last_failed) do NOT widen debt [029] -- verified against PostgreSQL source, and the reason should be recorded in the query
findings.description:
The feature puts two new server-supplied strings on the terminal (Data Models columns 3 and 6, last_archived_wal and last_failed_wal), which reach printDataCell unsanitised per debt [029]. Verified rather than assumed:

1. Those fields are populated only by pgstat_report_archiver(xlog, false) and pgstat_report_archiver(xlog, true) in src/backend/postmaster/pgarch.c. There is no SQL-reachable way to set them.
2. xlog is the basename returned by pgarch_readyXlog, which filters candidates with: `if (strspn(rlde->d_name, VALID_XFN_CHARS) < basenamelen) continue;` after `basenamelen = strlen(d_name) - 6` and a `.ready` suffix check.
3. src/include/postmaster/pgarch.h defines: `#define MIN_XFN_CHARS 16`, `#define MAX_XFN_CHARS 40`, `#define VALID_XFN_CHARS "0123456789ABCDEF.history.backup.partial"`.

That character set contains no ESC (0x1b), no CSI introducer, no control characters -- so no ANSI escape sequence can reach the terminal through these two columns, even from a hand-crafted .ready file placed by someone with OS write access to $PGDATA (such a file is skipped by the strspn filter and never reaches pgstat_report_archiver). Segment names are themselves generated by `snprintf(fname, MAXFNAMELEN, "%08X%08X%08X", ...)` (XLogFileName, src/include/access/xlog_internal.h). The remaining new columns are server-generated too: the three age columns are date_trunc(...)::text and column 0 is the SQL literal 'Archiver'.

Conclusion: this feature does not widen [029], including under pause, where 016 noted the self-healing argument weakens.
findings.location: Section: Data Models, archiver view columns 3 and 6; internal/query/archiver.go (new, Task 1)
findings.impact: None. Recorded so the conclusion is evidence-backed and does not have to be re-derived by the next reviewer, and so a future column addition sourced from a less constrained field (an object name, an application_name, a query text) is recognised as a different case.
findings.recommendation: Add one line to the archiver query's doc comment in internal/query/archiver.go stating that last_archived_wal / last_failed_wal are constrained by PostgreSQL to VALID_XFN_CHARS ("0123456789ABCDEF.history.backup.partial", 16-40 chars, enforced in pgarch_readyXlog) and therefore cannot carry escape sequences to the terminal -- unlike object names, which is what debt [029] is about. No sanitisation code is needed.

findings.title: -W string mapping must fail closed and must never return the raw flag value as the report type
findings.description:
Decision 7 turns -W into a string whose value selects a report type. The existing precedent in selectReport (cmd/report/report.go:132-200, used by -D, -J, -X, -P) is already correct and fails closed: an outer `case opts.showX != "":` guard with an inner exact-match switch that has no default, so an unrecognised value falls out of the switch entirely and the function returns "", which is caught at cmd/report/report.go:93-96 with 'report type is not specified, quit'. Task 4 must copy that shape verbatim.

The shape to avoid is returning opts.showWAL (or any value derived from it) as the report type, because ReportType is not inert downstream: it is the tar-entry name filter in isFilenameOK (report/report.go:460-476, `if s[0] != report && s[0] != "meta" && s[0] != "sysinfo"`), and it is a view.Views map key (`v := views[config.ReportType]`, report/report.go:85, and again at report.go:283/292 after a version change). An unmapped value passed through would yield a zero-value view.View (Ncols 0, empty DiffIntvl) and a run in which every tar entry is silently skipped -- no error, no rows -- rather than a clean failure. That is a fail-open shape on a path that consumes an operator-supplied archive file via -f.

The documented breaking-change behaviour is already fail-closed and was checked: `-W -f dump.tar` makes pflag consume '-f' as the value, so showWAL == "-f", no inner case matches, selectReport returns "", and the command exits non-zero with 'report type is not specified, quit'. Note that -f is consumed in that path, so the input file silently stays at its default -- harmless here only because the command aborts before reading it.
findings.location: cmd/report/report.go:151-152 (current bool case), cmd/report/report.go:93-96; report/report.go:85 and 460-476; Section: Decision 7, Task 4
findings.impact: If the mapping were implemented by passing the flag value through instead of whitelisting it, an operator typo or a scripted invocation would produce an empty, successful-looking report instead of an error, and the tar-entry filter would be driven by an unvalidated string. With the whitelist shape, unreachable.
findings.recommendation: Implement exactly as `case opts.showWAL != "":` + inner `switch opts.showWAL { case "w": return "wal"; case "a": return "archiver" }` with no default and no fallthrough returning the raw value. Extend the Task 4 tests beyond the planned `-W x` case: assert the resulting error string ('report type is not specified, quit'), not merely the empty return, and add cases for values that are valid letters for a different flag (`-W c`, `-W t`, `-W g`, `-W w` vs `-W W`) so a future shared letter-mapping helper cannot make one flag accept another's vocabulary.

findings.title: Decision 11 converts an unknown state into a confident zero in the verbose panel -- record the false-OK, do not revert the decision
findings.description: Decision 11 accepts that pg_ls_archive_statusdir() is missing_ok=true (confirmed in source: `return pg_ls_dir_files(fcinfo, XLOGDIR "/archive_status", true);`) whereas pg_ls_dir('pg_wal/archive_status') is missing_ok=false. The trade itself is settled and reasonable and is not being re-argued here. The residual worth recording is the shape of the new failure: a monitoring surface that previously rendered n/a ('I do not know') for a missing directory now renders a bold '0 B' ('there is no backlog'). A confident zero on a monitoring panel is a false-OK, which is the failure class A09 exists for -- an operator scanning the verbose panel during an incident reads 'archiving is fine' from a cluster whose archive_status is gone. The trigger is narrow (a damaged or hand-edited data directory; archive_status exists under archive_mode=off, so that common case is unaffected) and there is no cheap SQL-side fix, which is why the recommendation is to document rather than to change the design.
findings.impact: On a cluster with a missing or renamed pg_wal/archive_status, the verbose panel reports a confident 0 B backlog instead of n/a, so the panel gives a false all-clear for the one signal it was changed to improve. Requires an already-damaged data directory; no supported PostgreSQL configuration produces it.
findings.recommendation: No design change. Record the behaviour where an operator will find it: a tech-debt entry (or an explicit line in the 0.12.0 release notes alongside the other Decision 8 change) stating that after 0.12.0 a 0 B archiving backlog no longer distinguishes 'no backlog' from 'archive_status directory absent'. Keep the note in the query's doc comment too, since that is where the missing_ok difference lives.
